title: GreenFPGA: Evaluating FPGAs as Environmentally Sustainable Computing Solutions
problem: Quantifying the total lifecycle carbon footprint of FPGAs including manufacturing, operation, reconfigurability, disposal, and recycling to determine when reconfigurability benefits justify embodied carbon costs compared to ASICs.
motivation: Understanding and reducing the environmental impact of computing platforms is critical as climate concerns grow, and FPGAs' reconfigurability could offer sustainability advantages over application-specific hardware.
method: GreenFPGA calculates the total carbon emissions from FPGAs (programmable chips you can reprogram for different tasks) across their complete lifecycle, from manufacturing and operation through end-of-life options like disposal and recycling. It compares this against ASICs (chips designed for a single purpose) in different scenarios, with a focus on small production runs and short-lived applications—situations where being able to reprogram the FPGA instead of manufacturing new ASICs can reduce overall carbon footprint.
key_novelty: A tool that tracks the total carbon emissions from FPGAs (programmable chips you can reprogram) across their entire lifespan to show when this reusability reduces their carbon footprint compared to ASICs (single-purpose chips).
contributions: GreenFPGA tool for estimating total lifecycle carbon footprint of FPGAs
Evaluation framework comparing embodied and operational carbon costs of FPGAs versus ASICs
Demonstration that FPGAs have lower carbon footprint than ASICs for low-volume applications and short lifespans
Analysis of scenarios where reconfigurability benefits outweigh embodied carbon costs
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: Environmental sustainability of reconfigurable hardware through lifecycle analysis
